summary: This JUnit test checks the output that printStatusToDisplay() sends to the console. It temporarily redirects System.out into an in-memory buffer, calls the method, restores the real console, and then compares the captured text against the expected status line.

lines.text: A ByteArrayOutputStream collects bytes in memory instead of writing them to a file or the screen, which is what makes the printed output inspectable.
System.out is a PrintStream, so a replacement stream has to be that same type.
The earlier tests from this chapter still live in this class; only the new test is shown so the example stays short.
This annotation marks the method as a test case for JUnit to discover and run.
A thermostat at 72 degrees with eco mode off should be idle, which gives the test a predictable status line to expect.
Saving the real console stream first is essential, because the test must put it back afterwards or every later test would lose its output.
From this point on, anything printed with System.out.println goes into the buffer rather than to the terminal.
This is the call under test; its only observable effect is the text it prints.
A finally block runs even if the method under test throws, guaranteeing the console gets restored.
Restoring the original stream undoes the redirection so the rest of the test run behaves normally.
The expected value includes the platform's line separator because println adds a newline, and using System.lineSeparator() keeps the test passing on Windows as well as macOS and Linux.
